name: Double Down or Quit

positioning.oneLineSummary: Re-underwrites follow-on decisions from current evidence and fund opportunity cost rather than sunk cost.
positioning.productLabel: Follow-On Re-Underwriting Lens — based on The Venture Mindset public materials
notAClaimOf: a forced binary action in every case

attribution.display: Based on Ilya Strebulaev's public nine-principle keynote

neutralParaphrase: Each follow-on round should be evaluated as a fresh allocation decision using updated evidence, current price, ownership, reserves, alternatives, and original thesis milestones. Prior capital is sunk; progress can justify greater concentration, while unresolved or worsened risk can justify stopping. Practical actions include full follow-on, partial pro rata, bridge with milestones, hold, sell where possible, or stop.
requiredConditions: The original decision thesis and milestones are preserved.
Current company evidence, round terms, ownership, reserves, and alternatives are available.
The decision can be evaluated without treating prior investment as a reason to continue.

requiredEvidence.description: Decision-time thesis, milestones, risks, and falsifiers from the prior round.
Source-backed progress, misses, belief revisions, customer, product, economics, and team changes.
Current price, security, dilution, pro rata, liquidation terms, and ownership outcomes.
Reserve capacity and alternative uses of capital under the active Fund Policy.

decisionQuestions: Which original milestones were met, missed, or made irrelevant?
Did the most important uncertainty decrease?
At the new price, what return and ownership remain?
Is bridge capital buying a defined risk-reducing milestone or delaying recognition?
Which alternative use of reserves has the highest expected portfolio contribution?
What evidence supports full follow-on, partial follow-on, hold, or stop?
positiveSignals: Original high-risk assumptions were resolved with source-backed evidence.
The new round price still supports fund-return targets.
Additional capital buys a clear value-inflecting milestone.
The company improved quality without hiding changed assumptions.
Reserve use fits policy and dominates realistic alternatives.
redFlags: Prior investment is cited as a reason to protect the company.
Milestones were quietly rewritten after misses.
Bridge financing has no defined endpoint or new evidence target.
A headline up-round substitutes for business progress.
Pro rata is exercised automatically without price review.
The fund lacks reserves for stronger portfolio companies.
disconfirmingEvidence: The original key concern remains unresolved after material spend.
New capital primarily repays old obligations or extends runway without risk reduction.
A cheaper or stronger alternative use of capital exists.
Customer, margin, governance, or technical evidence deteriorated.
contraindications: Do not force every decision into a literal double-or-zero binary.
Do not include prior invested capital in the marginal go-forward cost.
Do not treat external round validation as company evidence.
Do not overwrite the original thesis.

instructions: Freeze and compare the original thesis with current evidence.
Re-run company quality, price, and fund fit independently.
Calculate ownership and reserve outcomes for each available action.
Choose among full, partial, conditional, hold, or stop actions under policy.

deterministicRule.calculationsOwnedBy: Scenario valuation, cap-table, and Fund Policy services

sourceReliability.low: The principle is known only through secondary summaries.
sourceReliability.medium: The official keynote supports the principle without chapter detail.
sourceReliability.high: Hashed keynote and reviewed licensed chapter converge.

evidenceStrength.low: Founder update and round signaling only.
evidenceStrength.medium: Original thesis and current operating evidence are available.
evidenceStrength.high: Original thesis, current evidence, price, ownership, reserves, and alternatives converge.

evidenceCoverage.low: Original thesis or current terms are missing.
evidenceCoverage.medium: Core evidence exists but opportunity cost or terms sensitivity is weak.
evidenceCoverage.high: All action scenarios and evidence deltas are documented.

applicabilityConfidence.medium: A follow-on exists but the fund has no meaningful choice.
applicabilityConfidence.high: Capital allocation and escalation risk are material.

judgmentConfidence.medium: Marginal attractiveness is estimable with unresolved price or reserve issues.
judgmentConfidence.high: Evidence, price, ownership, and opportunity cost support one action.

promotionRequirements: Define deterministic action scenarios in Fund Policy.
Backtest follow-on and stop decisions with original decision-time records.
Measure escalation-of-commitment errors and missed recovery cases.
empiricalQualifications: Follow-on availability and information are endogenous.
Outcomes are highly censored and long-dated.
Bridge rounds can be rational options or escalation depending on milestone design.

rights.notes: Only a neutral paraphrase of the public keynote principle is stored.

openIssues: Align with portfolio reserve and valuation services.

changeLog.summary: Initial draft turns double-down-or-quit into marginal re-underwriting.
